十四年春三月，軍至譙，作輕舟，治水軍。秋七月，自渦入淮，出肥水，軍合肥。辛未，令曰：「自頃已來，軍數征行，或遇疫氣，吏士死亡不歸，家室怨曠，百姓流離，而仁者豈樂之哉？不得已也。其令死者家無基業不能自存者，縣官勿絕廩，長吏存恤撫循，以稱吾意。」置揚州郡縣長吏，開芍陂屯田。十二月，軍還譙。

::: {.columns}

Fifteenth Year, Spring [210 Feb 12 – May 10], sent down Order: “Since antiquity of the lords that received the mandate or led an internal restoration, was there ever one who did not obtain worthy men and noble men to with them together govern Heaven’s Under? When they obtained the worthies, often they had not left their [hometown] alleys, so how was it by fortunately encountering one another? It was only by those above actively seeking them. Now Heaven’s Under is still not yet settled, this is the urgent time to especially seek the worthy. ‘Mèng Gōngchuò being an elder for Zhào or Wèi would be excellent, but he cannot be a grandee for Téng or Xuē.’  If one must certainly be an incorruptible servicemen and only after be employed, then how could Qí Huán have become hegemon over the world?  Now is Heaven’s Under without anyone hiding jade in plain clothes and fishing on the Wèi’s riverbank?  Also are there no one who stole his elder brother’s wife and accepted gold, but has not yet been discovered by [Wèi] Wúzhī?  You few sirs thus assist me in discovering and raising up the lowly and coarse. Only talent is to be nominated, I will obtain them and then employ them.”
Winter [210 Nov 5 – 211 Jan 31], built Tóngquètái. <a href="#annotation-75" id="source-75">[75]</a>

十五年春，下令曰：「自古受命及中興之君，曷嘗不得賢人君子與之共治天下者乎！及其得賢也，曾不出閭巷，豈幸相遇哉？上之人不求之耳。今天下尚未定，此特求賢之急時也。『孟公綽為趙、魏老則優，不可以為滕、薛大夫』。若必廉士而後可用，則齊桓其何以霸世！今天下得無有被褐懷玉而釣于渭濱者乎？又得無盜嫂受金而未遇無知者乎？二三子其佐我明揚仄陋，唯才是舉，吾得而用之。」冬，作銅雀臺。〔一〕

<a href="#source-75" id="annotation-75">[75]</a> Wèi Wǔ Gùshì records the Excellency’s Twelfth Moon Jǐhài  Order: “When I  was first nominated as a Filial-Incorruptible, my years were few, I myself believed that I was not a serviceman of fame living in a cave,  feared that I would be viewed by the people Within the Seas as a common fool, and wished to be an administrator of a single prefecture, wanting to do well in governance and instruction, to establish a reputation, and have the servicemen of the world know of it. Therefore in Jǐnán, I began by eliminating the oppressive and removing the corrupt, with fair judgment in selection and nomination, opposing and offending the various Regular Attendants. As I was hated by the strong and powerful, fearing it would bring disaster on my family, therefore I plead illness and resigned. After leaving office, my years of age were still few, and looking back to those of my same [nomination] year, there were those of fifty years who were not yet called as old, and inside I considered this, that from then I could retire for twenty years and wait for Heaven’s Under to be purified, and then be the same as those first nominated in my year. Therefore for the four seasons I remained in my hometown, to the east of Qiáo by fifty lǐ built a study house,  wishing to in the autumn and summer read books, in the winter and spring shoot and hunt, seeking barren land, wishing to conceal myself in mud and water, cutting off from expectations of comings and goings and guests and visitors, but was not able to obtain my intentions. Later I was summoned as a Commandant, promoted to Organizing Army Colonel, my intentions therefore changed and I wished to serve the country in suppressing rebels and establishing achievement, wishing and hoping to be enfeoffed a Marquess and be a Campaigning West General,  and afterwards the sign on the road to my tomb would say: ‘Hàn’s former Campaigning West General, Marquess Cáo’s Tomb.’ This was the ambition. But happening to encounter the trouble of Dǒng Zhuó, I raised Righteous Troops. At the time in gathering troops it was possible to obtain more, however I always restrained myself, not wishing to have too many. The reason for this was that too many troops leads to arrogance, and fighting with powerful enemies might lead to further creation of disasters. Therefore at the Battle of Biàn River there were only a few thousand, and afterward returning to arrive at Yáng Province to again recruit, it also again did not exceed three thousand men. This was that my original ambitions had limits. Later I was designated Yǎn Province, defeated and accepted the surrenders of Huángjīn multitudes of three hundred thousand. Also Yuán Shù usurped titles in Jiǔjiāng, his subordinates all declared themselves his subjects, he named his gates Jiànhào Gate,  his clothes and coverings all were by the standards of Heaven’s Son, his two wives in advance fought over becoming Imperial Empress. His ambitions and plans were already settled, someone advised [Yuán] Shù to therefore ascend the Emperor’s Throne and announce it to Heaven’s Under, he answered saying: ‘Excellency Cáo is still here, it cannot yet be.’  Later I suppressed and destroyed his four Generals, captured his men and multitudes, therefore causing [Yuán] Shù to end as a destitute exile, and he fell ill and died. By then Yuán Shào had occupied the Hé’s north, his military power strong and flourishing, I measured my own power as truly no match for his, however I calculated that throwing myself into death for the country, sacrificing myself for righteousness, was enough to bequeath to posterity. By good fortune yet I defeated [Yuán] Shào and destroyed his two sons. Also Liú Biǎo believed himself part of the Imperial Clan but yet concealed a treacherous heart,  suddenly advancing suddenly retreating, by this watching the situation of the world, occupying and possessing his province. I also settled him, and therefore pacified Heaven’s Under. I have become the foremost minister, among servants of men I am already at the utmost in nobility, my intentions and hopes already surpassed. Now I say this, appearing very self-arrogant, [but] wishing people to discuss it thoroughly, therefore there is nothing I avoid mentioning: Supposing if the country had been without me, it is unknown how many men would have declared themselves Emperors, how many men declared themselves Kings. Perhaps there are people who observe that my power is flourishing, and also by nature I do not believe in the matters of Heaven’s Mandate, and fear that private hearts will judge, saying that I have inappropriate ambitions, making absurd speculations and contemplations, and I am always troubled by this.  The reason Qí Huán and Jìn Wén are praised to the present day is that although their military power was expansive and great, they yet were able to respectfully serve the Zhōu House.  The Lúnyǔ says: ‘Of three parts of Heaven’s Under possessing two yet serving Yīn, Zhōu’s virtue can be said to be utmost virtue.’  This was the ability to use the great to serve the small. In the past Yuè Yì fled to Zhào, the King of Zhào wished to with him plan against Yān,  Yuè Yì in prostration shed tears, replied saying: ‘Your Servant served [Yān] King Zhāo just as I serve you Heavenly King. If Your Servant had a crime and was banished to another state, to the end of my life I could not bear to plan against the lowliest retainers of Zhào, so all the more for the later successor of Yān!’ When Húhài killed Méng Tián, [Méng] Tián said: ‘From my ancestors to my descendants, our accumulated faith to Qín has reached three generations. Now Your Servant commands troops of over three hundred thousand, and this power is sufficient for rebellion, however that I know that I must die to uphold righteousness, is that I do not dare disgrace the teachings of my ancestors or forget the Former King.’  Every time I read the stories of these two men, never once I have not grieved and shed tears. My grandfather to my own person all held intimate and important appointments, and can be said to have met with faith, and reaching to Zǐhuán and his brothers, we have passed three generations.  I do not only say this to you sirs. I always speak to my wife and concubines, to have them all deeply understand these intentions. I say to them: ‘After my ten thousand years,  you should all go out and remarry. I wish to have you tell of my heart, so that other men all understand it.’ I say all this from the bottom of my heart.  The reason I diligently and earnestly explain my heart, is that I have observed how Zhōu-gōng had a letter in a metal coffer to prove himself because he feared that people would not believe him.  However the wish for me to transfer and relinquish the troops and multitudes I command to return control over affairs, and retire to my fief as Marquess of Wǔpíng, it truly cannot be. Why? Honestly, I fear that after I leave my troops I would come to harm by someone. This is planning for my descendants, and also that if I am destroyed then the country would be endangered. Therefore, I will not admire empty reputation to seek real disaster. This cannot be done. Formerly, the Court generously enfeoffed three of my sons as Marquesses, but I firmly declined and would not accept. Now I instead wish to accept this, not from a wish for further glory, but a wish to have them be outer assistance, to be a plan for complete security. I have heard of Jiè Tuī avoiding fief from Jìn  and Shēn Xū fleeing from reward from Chǔ,  and never once have I not set down my books and sighed, and by this examined myself. Serving the state’s authority and prestige, I wield battle-ax on campaign, for the weak subduing the strong, for the small seizing the great. Of what was planned in thought, in action there was no failure in affairs. Of what was considered in heart, what direction was not relieved? Therefore in cleansing and pacifying Heaven’s Under, not disgracing the ruler’s command, it can be said that it was Heaven that assisted the Hàn House, not the strength of men. However my fief contains four counties, income of thirty thousand households; what virtue is worthy of this? The rivers and lakes are not yet tranquil, so I cannot resign my position, but as for fief territory, it can be ceded. Now I return up Yángxià, Zhè, Kǔ,  three counties and twenty thousand households, only keeping revenue from Wǔpíng’s ten thousand households, to for a while decrease slanderous comments and slightly reduce the censure on me.”

〔一〕　魏武故事載公十二月己亥令曰：「孤始舉孝廉，年少，自以本非巖穴知名之士，恐為海內人之所見凡愚，欲為一郡守，好作政教，以建立名譽，使世士明知之；故在濟南，始除殘去穢，平心選舉，違迕諸常侍。以為彊豪所忿，恐致家禍，故以病還。去官之後，年紀尚少，顧視同歲中，年有五十，未名為老，內自圖之，從此卻去二十年，待天下清，乃與同歲中始舉者等耳。故以四時歸鄉里，於譙東五十里築精舍，欲秋夏讀書，冬春射獵，求底下之地，欲以泥水自蔽，絕賓客往來之望，然不能得如意。後徵為都尉，遷典軍校尉，意遂更欲為國家討賊立功，欲望封侯作征西將軍，然後題墓道言『漢故征西將軍曹侯之墓』，此其志也。而遭值董卓之難，興舉義兵。是時合兵能多得耳，然常自損，不欲多之；所以然者，多兵意盛，與彊敵爭，倘更為禍始。故汴水之戰數千，後還到揚州更募，亦復不過三千人，此其本志有限也。後領兗州，破降黃巾三十萬眾。又袁術僭號于九江，下皆稱臣，名門曰建號門，衣被皆為天子之制，兩婦預爭為皇后。志計已定，人有勸術使遂即帝位，露布天下，答言『曹公尚在，未可也』。後孤討禽其四將，獲其人眾，遂使術窮亡解沮，發病而死。及至袁紹據河北，兵勢彊盛，孤自度勢，實不敵之，但計投死為國，以義滅身，足垂於後。幸而破紹，梟其二子。又劉表自以為宗室，包藏姦心，乍前乍卻，以觀世事，據有當州，孤復定之，遂平天下。身為宰相，人臣之貴已極，意望已過矣。今孤言此，若為自大，欲人言盡，故無諱耳。設使國家無有孤，不知當幾人稱帝，幾人稱王。或者人見孤彊盛，又性不信天命之事，恐私心相評，言有不遜之志，妄相忖度，每用耿耿。齊桓、晉文所以垂稱至今日者，以其兵勢廣大，猶能奉事周室也。論語云『三分天下有其二，以服事殷，周之德可謂至德矣』，夫能以大事小也。昔樂毅走趙，趙王欲與之圖燕，樂毅伏而垂泣，對曰：『臣事昭王，猶事天王；臣若獲戾，放在他國，沒世然後已，不忍謀趙之徒隸，況燕後嗣乎！』胡亥之殺蒙恬也，恬曰：『自吾先人及至子孫，積信於秦三世矣；今臣將兵三十餘萬，其勢足以背叛，然自知必死而守義者，不敢辱先人之教以忘先王也。』孤每讀此二人書，未嘗不愴然流涕也。孤祖父以至孤身，皆當親重之任，可謂見信者矣，以及（子植）〔子桓〕兄弟，過于三世矣。孤非徒對諸君說此也，常以語妻妾，皆令深知此意。孤謂之言：『顧我萬年之後，汝曹皆當出嫁，欲令傳道我心，使他人皆知之。』孤此言皆肝鬲之要也。所以勤勤懇懇敘心腹者，見周公有金縢之書以自明，恐人不信之故。然欲孤便爾委捐所典兵眾以還執事，歸就武平侯國，實不可也。何者？誠恐己離兵為人所禍也。既為子孫計，又己敗則國家傾危，是以不得慕虛名而處實禍，此所不得為也。前朝恩封三子為侯，固辭不受，今更欲受之，非欲復以為榮，欲以為外援，為萬安計。孤聞介推之避晉封。申胥之逃楚賞，未嘗不舍書而歎，有以自省也。奉國威靈，仗鉞征伐，推弱以克彊，處小而禽大，意之所圖，動無違事，心之所慮，何向不濟，遂蕩平天下，不辱主命，可謂天助漢室，非人力也。然封兼四縣，食戶三萬，何德堪之！江湖未靜，不可讓位；至于邑土，可得而辭。今上還陽夏、柘、苦三縣戶二萬，但食武平萬戶，且以分損謗議，少減孤之責也。」
