::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Winter, Tenth Moon [216 Oct 29 – Nov 26], Drilled Troops, <a href="#annotation-108" id="source-108">[108]</a> therefore campaigned against Sūn Quán. Eleventh Moon [216 Nov 27 – Dec 26], reached Qiáo.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
冬十月，治兵，〔一〕遂征孫權，十一月至譙。
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-108" id="annotation-108">[108]</a> Wèi shū states: The King personally beat the metal and drums to order the advances and withdrawals.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔一〕　魏書曰：王親執金鼓以令進退。
:::
:::
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Twenty-Second Year, Spring, Standard Moon [217 Jan 25 – Feb 23], the King’s army at Jūcháo, Second Moon [217 Feb 24 – Mar 24], advanced the army to garrison the Jiāng’s west’s Hǎoxī.  [Sūn] Quán at Rúxūkǒu built fortifications to resist and defend, therefore pressured and attacked him, [Sūn] Quán retreated and fled.
Third Moon [217 Mar 25 – Apr 23], the King led the army to return, left Xiàhóu Dūn, Cáo Rén, Zhāng Liáo, and others to garrison Jūcháo.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
二十二年春正月，王軍居巢，二月，進軍屯江西郝谿。權在濡須口築城拒守，遂逼攻之，權退走。三月，王引軍還，留夏侯惇、曹仁、張遼等屯居巢。
:::
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Summer, Fourth Moon [217 May 24 – Jun 21], Heaven’s Son mandated that the King set up the flags and banners of Heaven’s Son, in going out and in to order to clear the streets. 
Fifth Moon [217 Jun 21 – Jul 21], built Pàn’gōng. 
Sixth Moon [217 Jul 22 – Aug 19], appointed Army Preceptor Huà Xīn as Censorate Grandee. <a href="#annotation-109" id="source-109">[109]</a>
Winter, Tenth Moon [217 Nov 17 – Dec 15], Heaven’s Son mandated that the King wear cap of ten and two tassels, ride Gold Root chariot drawn by Six Horses, set Five Seasons Escort Carriages.  Appointed Five Office Central Cadet General [Cáo] Pī as Wèi Heir-Apparent.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
夏四月，天子命王設天子旌旗，出入稱警蹕。五月，作泮宮。六月，以軍師華歆為御史大夫。〔一〕冬十月，天子命王冕十有二旒，乘金根車，駕六馬，設五時副車，以五官中郎將丕為魏太子。
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-109" id="annotation-109">[109]</a> Wèi shū states: First installed the Minister of the Guard office. Autumn, Eighth Moon [217 Sep 19 – Oct 17], Order said: “In the past Yī Zhì, Fù Yuè came from among the poor people,  Guǎn Zhòng was Duke Huán’s enemy,  all were employed to bring prosperity. Xiāo Hé, Cáo Cān were county clerks,  Hán [Xìn], Chén Píng carried dirtied and disgraced names, had the shame of being met with ridicule,  but in the end were able to achieve the ruler’s enterprise, reputation known for a thousand years. Wú Qǐ  was a rapacious officer, killed his wife to prove himself, spent gold to seek office, when his mother died he did not return home; however, when he was at Wèi, the Qín people did not dare head east, and when he was at Chǔ then the Three Jìn  did not dare plot south. Now Under Heaven are there no people of utmost virtue stranded among the civilians, as well as the resolute and valorous who do not look back when facing the enemy and fiercely battling? Or common civil clerks, high in talent and strange in character, perhaps able to be officers and administrators? Carrying dirtied and disgraced names, meeting with ridicule for conduct, perhaps not benevolent or not filial but yet have the skills to govern state or employ soldiers? Thus each are to nominate those they know, and do not have omissions.”
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔一〕　魏書曰：初置衛尉官。秋八月，令曰：「昔伊摯、傅說出於賤人，管仲，桓公賊也，皆用之以興。蕭何、曹參，縣吏也，韓、陳平負汙辱之名，有見笑之恥，卒能成就王業，聲著千載。吳起貪將，殺妻自信，散金求官，母死不歸，然在魏，奏人不敢東向，在楚則三晉不敢南謀。今天下得無有至德之人放在民間，及果勇不顧，臨敵力戰；若文俗之吏，高才異質，或堪為將守；負汙辱之名，見笑之行，或不仁不孝而有治國用兵之術：其各舉所知，勿有所遺。」
:::
:::
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Liú Bèi sent Zhāng Fēi, Mǎ Chāo, Wú Lán,  and others to garrison Xiàbiàn.  Sent Cáo Hóng to resist them.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
劉備遣張飛、馬超、吳蘭等屯下辯；遣曹洪拒之。
:::
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Twenty-Third Year, Spring, Standard Moon [218 Feb 13 – Mar 14], Hàn Grand Physician Director Jí Běn with Minister Treasurer Gěng Jì and Manager of Standards Wéi Huǎng and others rebelled,  attacked Xǔ, burned Assistant Chancellor’s Chief Scribe Wáng Bì’s barracks. <a href="#annotation-110" id="source-110">[110]</a> [Wáng] Bì with Yǐngchuān Managing Agriculture Central Cadet-General Yán Kuāng  suppressed and beheaded them. <a href="#annotation-111" id="source-111">[111]</a>
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
二十三年春正月，漢太醫令吉本與少府耿紀、司直韋晃等反，攻許，燒丞相長史王必營，〔一〕必與潁川典農中郎將嚴匡討斬之〔二〕。
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-110" id="annotation-110">[110]</a> Wèi Wǔ Gùshì records an Order stating: “Designate Chief Scribe Wáng Bì was my clerk from the time I was chopping thistles and thorns,  loyal and capable and diligent in matters, heart like iron and stone, the state’s excellent clerk. The misstep of not recruiting him for a long time, was abandoning a fine stallion and not riding it; why hurriedly and anxiously again seek another? Therefore instruct to recruit him, having already arranged an appropriate position, and have him as Designate Chief Scribe manage matters as before.”
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔一〕　魏武故事載令曰：「領長史王必，是吾披荊棘時吏也。忠能勤事，心如鐵石，國之良吏也。蹉跌久未辟之，捨騏驥而弗乘，焉遑遑而更求哉？故教辟之，已署所宜，便以領長史統事如故。」
:::
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-111" id="annotation-111">[111]</a> Sānfǔ Juélù zhù  states: At the time there was Jīngzhào’s Jīn Yī appellation Déyī,  himself believed [his family] for generations had been Hàn ministers, from since [Jīn] Mìdī had suppressed Mǎng Héluó,  loyalty and sincerity demonstrably shown, reputation and integrity for accumulated ages. Observing that Hàn’s blessings were about to be removed, he said there could be third rising,  and thus sighed in indignation, and therefore with Gěng Jì, Wéi Huǎng, Jí Běn, [Jí] Běn’s son [Jí] Miǎo, [Jí] Miǎo’s younger brother [Jí] Mù  and others joined and planned. [Gěng] Jì appellation Jìxíng,  in youth had beautiful reputation, became an Assistant Chancellor’s Official, the King extremely respected and was impressed with him, promoted to Attendant Central, observing Minister Treasurer. [Jí] Miǎo appellation Wénrán, [Jí] Mù appellation Sīrán,  as [Jīn] Yī was fervent and had resemblance to [Jīn] Mìdī, and also was friendly with Wáng Bì, took advantage to have him infiltrate them, to kill [Wáng] Bì, wishing to seize Heaven’s Son to attack Wèi and to the south assist Liú Bèi. At the time Guān Yǔ was strong and flourishing, while the King was at Yè, leaving [Wáng] Bì to manage troops and command matters in Xǔ.  [Jí Miǎo] Wénrán and the rest led miscellaneous people and house servants of over a thousand men in the night to burn the gates and attack [Wáng] Bì, [Jīn] Yī sent men to answer from the inside, shooting [Wáng] Bì in the shoulder. [Wáng] Bì did not know who the attackers were, and as he was previously friendly with [Jīn] Yī, fled to take refuge with [Jīn] Yī, in the night shouting “Déyī.” [Jīn] Yī’s household did not know it was [Wáng] Bì, said it was Wénrán and the rest, and mistakenly answered saying: “Is Chief Scribe Wáng already dead? Your matter is achieved!” [Wáng] Bì thus again fled on another road. Another account states: [Wáng] Bì wished to take refuge with [Jīn] Yī, his bannermen supervisor said to [Wáng] Bì: “In today’s affairs do you really know whose gates you can flee into?” Supporting [Wáng] Bì they fled over the south city wall. It happened it was dawn, [Wáng] Bì was still alive, Wénrán and the rest’s multitudes scattered, and therefore were destroyed. After over ten days, [Wáng] Bì indeed died from his wounds.

Xiàn-dì Chūnqiū states: Arrested [Gěng] Jì and [Wéi] Huǎng and the rest, about to behead them, [Gěng] Jì shouted the King of Wèi’s personal name,  saying: “I only regret that I did not have my own plan, and indeed was misled by a few boys!” [Wéi] Huǎng knocked his head [to the ground] and beat his mouth until he died.

Shānyáng-gōng Zàijì states: The King heard that Wáng Bì had died, was overwhelmingly furious, summoned Hàn’s Hundred Officials  to visit Yè, ordered those that fought the fire to the left, those that did not fight the fire to the right. The multitudes all believed those that fought the fire certainly would be without punishment, and all went left. The King believed: “Those that did not fight the fire did not add to the chaos, those that fought the fire thus are the real rebels.” Killed them all.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔二〕　三輔決錄注曰：時有京兆金禕字德禕，自以世為漢臣，自日磾討莽何羅，忠誠顯著，名節累葉。睹漢祚將移，謂可季興，乃喟然發憤，遂與耿紀、韋晃、吉本、本子邈、邈弟穆等結謀。紀字季行，少有美名，為丞相掾，王甚敬異之，遷侍中，守少府。邈字文然，穆字思然，以禕慷慨有日磾之風，又與王必善，因以閒之，若殺必，欲挾天子以攻魏，南援劉備。時關羽彊盛，而王在鄴，留必典兵督許中事。文然等率雜人及家僮千餘人夜燒門攻必，禕遣人為內應，射必中肩。必不知攻者為誰，以素與禕善，走投禕，夜喚德禕，禕家不知是必，謂為文然等，錯應曰：「王長史已死乎？卿曹事立矣！」必乃更他路奔。一曰：必欲投禕，其帳下督謂必曰：「今日事竟知誰門而投入乎？」扶必奔南城。會天明，必猶在，文然等眾散，故敗。後十餘日，必竟以創死。獻帝春秋曰：收紀、晃等，將斬之，紀呼魏王名曰：「恨吾不自生意，竟為群兒所誤耳！」晃頓首搏頰，以至於死。山陽公載記曰：王聞王必死，盛怒，召漢百官詣鄴，令救火者左，不救火者右。眾人以為救火者必無罪，皆附左；王以為「不救火者非助亂，救火乃實賊也」。皆殺之。
:::
:::
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Cáo Hóng defeated Wú Lán, beheaded his officer Rèn Kuí and others.  Third Moon [218 Apr 13 – May 12], Zhāng Fēi and Mǎ Chāo fled Hànzhōng, Yīnpíng’s Dī [man] Qiángduān beheaded Wú Lán and sent his head.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
曹洪破吳蘭，斬其將任夔等。三月，張飛、馬超走漢中，陰平氐強端斬吳蘭，傳其首。
:::
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Summer, Fourth Moon [218 May 13 – Jun 10], Dài Prefecture and Shànggǔ’s Wūhuán Wúchéndī and others rebelled.  Sent the Marquess of Yānlíng [Cáo] Zhāng  to suppress, defeated them. <a href="#annotation-112" id="source-112">[112]</a>
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
夏四月，代郡、上谷烏丸無臣氐等叛，遣鄢陵侯彰討破之。〔一〕
:::
:::


::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-112" id="annotation-112">[112]</a> Wèi shū records the King’s Order stating: “Last winter, Heaven sent down plague, the people suffered injuries, the army was mobilized in the exterior, cultivated farmland was reduced, I am extremely anxious of this. Thus order officials and civilians, male and female: women aged seventy and above with no husband or sons, or aged twelve and below with no father or mother or brothers, or those with eyes that cannot see, hands that cannot work, legs that cannot walk, and with no wives or children or fathers or elder brothers or property, government granaries are to feed them to the end of their lives, the young reaching until twelve. The poor unable to provide for themselves by mouths [per household] are given loans. For the aged and senile that must have caretakers, aged ninety and above, give labor exemptions of one person per family.”
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔一〕　魏書載王令曰：「去冬天降疫癘，民有凋傷，軍興於外，墾田損少，吾甚憂之。其令吏民男女：女年七十已上無夫子，若年十二已下無父母兄弟，及目無所見，手不能作，足不能行，而無妻子父兄產業者，廩食終身。幼者至十二止，貧窮不能自贍者，隨口給貸。老耄須待養者，年九十已上，復不事，家一人。」
:::
:::
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Sixth Moon [218 Jul 11 – Aug 8], Order said: “The ancients in burials were certain to occupy barren ground. Thus take Xīmén Bào’s  shrine’s west highland for the funerary tomb,  taking advantage of the heights for foundation, no mound no trees.  By the Zhōu Lǐ: ‘the Grave Master handles public burial ground,’  overall the vassal lords occupy the left and right of the front, ministers and grandees occupy the rear, Hàn’s system also called these as Accompanying Tombs.  Thus the Excellencies and Ministers and great officials and ranked officers with achievements, should accompany the funerary tomb. Thus expand the area, to allow sufficient space.”
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
六月，令曰：「古之葬者，必居瘠薄之地。其規西門豹祠西原上為壽陵，因高為基，不封不樹。周禮冢人掌公墓之地，凡諸侯居左右以前，卿大夫居後，漢制亦謂之陪陵。其公卿大臣列將有功者，宜陪壽陵，其廣為兆域，使足相容。」
:::
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Autumn, Seventh Moon [218 Aug 9 – Sep 7], Drilled Troops, therefore campaigned west against Liú Bèi. Ninth Moon [Oct 8 – Nov 5], reached Cháng’ān.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
秋七月，治兵，遂西征劉備，九月，至長安。
:::
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Winter, Tenth Moon [218 Nov 6 – Dec 5], Wǎn’s defending officer Hóu Yīn and others rebelled,  seized the Nányáng Administrator, robbed and plundered the officials and civilians, protected Wǎn. Previously, Cáo Rén suppressed Guān Yǔ and garrisoned Fánchéng.  That moon sent [Cáo] Rén to besiege Wǎn.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
冬十月，宛守將侯音等反，執南陽太守，劫略吏民，保宛。初，曹仁討關羽，屯樊城，是月使仁圍宛。
:::
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Twenty-Fourth Year, Spring, Standard Moon [219 Feb 3 – Mar 3], [Cáo] Rén slaughtered Wǎn, beheaded [Hóu] Yīn. <a href="#annotation-113" id="source-113">[113]</a>
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
二十四年春正月，仁屠宛，斬音。〔一〕
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-113" id="annotation-113">[113]</a> Cáo Mán zhuàn states: At that time Nányáng was suffering from conscripted labor, [Hóu] Yīn therefore seized Administrator Dōnglǐ Gǔn,  with officials and civilians together rebelling, with Guān Yǔ joining in alliance. Nányáng Merit Officer Zōng Zǐqīng  went to persuade [Hóu] Yīn saying: “You sir follow the people’s hearts, raising a great affair, far and near none do not watch the winds. However, seizing the prefecture officer is adverse and without benefit. Why not send him away? I will join strength with you, and by the time Excellency Cáo’s army comes, Guān Yǔ’s troops also will have arrived.” [Hóu] Yīn followed this, at once releasing and sending the Administrator. Zǐqīng took advantage in the night to go over the city walls to flee out, and therefore with the Administrator collected the remaining people to besiege [Hóu] Yīn. It happened that Cáo Rén’s army arrived, and together they exterminated them.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔一〕　曹瞞傳曰：是時南陽閒苦繇役，音於是執太守（東里裦）〔東里袞〕，與吏民共反，與關羽連和。南陽功曹宗子卿往說音曰：「足下順民心，舉大事，遠近莫不望風；然執郡將，逆而無益，何不遣之。吾與子共戮力，比曹公軍來，關羽兵亦至矣。」音從之，即釋遣太守。子卿因夜踰城亡出，遂與太守收餘民圍音，會曹仁軍至，共滅之。
:::
:::
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Xiàhóu Yuān with Liú Bèi battled at Yángpíng and was by [Liú] Bèi killed.  Third Moon [219 Apr 3 – May 1], the King from Cháng’ān set out Yégǔ,  the army screened the critical points to overlook Hànzhōng, and therefore reached Yángpíng. [Liú] Bèi took advantage of the difficult terrain to resist and defend. <a href="#annotation-114" id="source-114">[114]</a>
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
夏侯淵與劉備戰於陽平，為備所殺。三月，王自長安出斜谷，軍遮要以臨漢中，遂至陽平。備因險拒守。〔一〕
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-114" id="annotation-114">[114]</a> Jiǔzhōu Chūnqiū states: At the time the King wished to return, and sent out an Order that said: “Chicken Rib.” The office associates did not know what it was saying. Registrar Yáng Xiū  then on his own packed. Someone was alarmed and asked [Yáng] Xiū: “How did you understand it?” [Yáng] Xiū said: “Chicken ribs, to discard them is a shame, to eat them has no gain. Comparing this to Hànzhōng, one knows the King wishes to return.”
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔一〕　九州春秋曰：時王欲還，出令曰「雞肋」，官屬不知所謂。主簿楊脩便自嚴裝，人驚問脩：「何以知之？」脩曰：「夫雞肋，棄之如可惜，食之無所得，以比漢中，知王欲還也。」
:::
:::
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Summer, Fifth Moon [219 Jun 1 – Jun 29], led the army back to Cháng’ān.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
夏五月，引軍還長安。
:::
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Autumn, Seventh Moon [219 Jul 30 – Aug 27], appointed the consort Biàn-shì as Royal Queen.  Sent Yú Jīn to assist Cáo Rén in striking Guān Yǔ. Eighth Moon [219 Aug 28 – Sep 26], the Hàn river flooded, drowning [Yú] Jīn’s army. The army was destroyed, [Guān] Yǔ captured [Yú] Jīn and therefore besieged [Cáo] Rén. Sent Xú Huǎng to rescue him.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
秋七月，以夫人卞氏為王后。遣于禁助曹仁擊關羽。八月，漢水溢，灌禁軍，軍沒，羽獲禁，遂圍仁。使徐晃救之。
:::
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Ninth Moon [219 Sep 27 – Oct 25], Chancellor of State Zhōng Yáo in connection to West Department Official Wèi Fěng’s rebellion was dismissed. <a href="#annotation-115" id="source-115">[115]</a>
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
九月，相國鍾繇坐西曹掾魏諷反免。〔一〕
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-115" id="annotation-115">[115]</a> Shìyǔ states: [Wèi] Fěng appellation Zǐjīng  was a Pèi man, had talent in captivating the masses, admired and active in Yè capital, Zhōng Yáo because of this recruited him. The main army had not yet returned, [Wèi] Fěng secretly joined with followers and faction, and also with Chánglè Minister of the Guard Chén Yī  planned to attack Yè. Before the planned time, [Chén] Yī was afraid and reported it to the Heir-Apparent [Cáo Pī]. Executed [Wèi] Fěng, those connected that died were several tens of men.

Wáng Chǎng’s Jiājiè  states: “Jǐyīn’s Wèi Fěng,” but this says “Pèi man.” It is uncertain.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔一〕　世語曰：諷字子京，沛人，有惑眾才，傾動鄴都，鍾繇由是辟焉。大軍未反，諷潛結徒黨，又與長樂衛尉陳禕謀襲鄴。未及期，禕懼，告之太子，誅諷，坐死者數十人。王昶家誡曰「濟陰魏諷」，而此云沛人，未詳。
:::
:::
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Winter, Tenth Moon [219 Oct 26 – Nov 24], the army returned to Luòyáng. <a href="#annotation-116" id="source-116">[116]</a> Sūn Quán sent envoy to send up letter to request to suppress Guān Yǔ to prove himself. The King from Luòyáng campaigned south against [Guān] Yǔ, had not yet arrived, [Xú] Huǎng attacked [Guān] Yǔ, defeated him, [Guān] Yǔ fled, [Cáo] Rén’s besiegement was resolved. The King’s army at Móbēi. <a href="#annotation-117" id="source-117">[117]</a>
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
冬十月，軍還洛陽。〔一〕孫權遣使上書，以討關羽自效。王自洛陽南征羽，未至，晃攻羽，破之，羽走，仁圍解。王軍摩陂。〔二〕
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-116" id="annotation-116">[116]</a> Cáo Mán zhuàn states: The King rebuilt the North Division Commandant Office, ordering it surpass its former state.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔一〕　曹瞞傳曰：王更脩治北部尉廨，令過于舊。
:::
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-117" id="annotation-117">[117]</a> Wèi lüè states: Sūn Quán sent up letter declaring himself subject, declaring and explaining Heaven’s Mandate. The King had [Sūn] Quán’s letter shown to the exterior, saying: “This boy wishes to put me above the stove fire!”  Attendant Central Chén Qún and Secretariat Writer Huán Jiē  memorialized stating: “Hàn from since Emperor Ān onward had governance leave the ruling house, the state’s succession was repeatedly severed.  Reaching to the present, there is only the name and title. A chǐ of land or a single civilian, all are not Hàn’s possession. Its allotted fate for a long time has already been exhausted, the calendar calculations for a long time have already ended.  It is not only on today. Therefore, during Huán and Líng,  those that observed and understood the Tú and Wĕi  all said: ‘Hàn’s transition aura is exhausted, the Yellow House shall rise.’ Your Highness  answers this allotment, of the ten divisions of Heaven’s Under then possessing nine, to submit and serve Hàn, the crowds take note and watch, far and near complain and sigh, and therefore Sūn Quán from afar declares himself subject, this is the answering of Heaven and Man, different auras together in chorus. Your Servants humbly believe Yú and Xià did not modestly decline,  Yīn and Zhōu did not begrudge executing and exiling.  Fearing Heaven and understanding the Mandate, there is no reason to decline.”

Wèishì Chūnqiū states: Xiàhóu Dūn said to the King: “Heaven’s Under all knows Hàn’s blessings are already exhausted, a different dynasty is about to rise. Since antiquity onward, the one able to remove the people’s sufferings and to which the Hundred Surnames submit to, is exactly the ruler of the people. Now Your Highness has fought in war for over thirty years, achievements and virtues known to the numerous masses, the one Heaven’s Under depends on and submits to. In answering Heaven and obeying the people, what further is there to doubt?” The King said: “‘Displaying it in government, is also to be government.’  If Heaven’s Mandate is with me, I am Zhōu Wén-wáng.” 

Cáo Mán zhuàn and Shìyǔ both say Huán Jiē urged the King to correct his rank,  Xiàhóu Dūn believed: “It is appropriate to first exterminate Shǔ, if Shǔ is destroyed then Wú will submit, two regions then settled, and only afterward follow the path of Shùn and Yǔ.”  The King followed this. When the King died, [Xiàhóu] Dūn regretted his previous words, fell ill and died.

Sūn Shèng’s Appraisal states: Xiàhóu Dūn was ashamed to be a Hàn official and requested to receive a Wèi seal.  Huán Jiē was proper and honest, having righteous and upright integrity. Investigating their biography records, Shìyǔ is absurd.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔二〕　魏略曰：孫權上書稱臣，稱說天命。王以權書示外曰：「是兒欲踞吾著爐火上邪！」侍中陳群、尚書桓階奏曰：「漢自安帝已來，政去公室，國統數絕，至於今者，唯有名號，尺土一民，皆非漢有，期運久已盡，曆數久已終，非適今日也。是以桓、靈之間，諸明圖緯者，皆言『漢行氣盡，黃家當興』。殿下應期，十分天下而有其九，以服事漢，群生注望，，遐邇怨歎，是故孫權在遠稱臣，此天人之應，異氣齊聲。臣愚以為虞、夏不以謙辭，殷、周不吝誅放，畏天知命，無所與讓也。」魏氏春秋曰：夏侯惇謂王曰：「天下咸知漢祚已盡，異代方起。自古已來，能除民害為百姓所歸者，即民主也。今殿下即戎三十餘年，功德著於黎庶，為天下所依歸，應天順民，復何疑哉！」王曰：「『施于有政，是亦為政』。若天命在吾，吾為周文王矣。」曹瞞傳及世語並云桓階勸王正位，夏侯惇以為宜先滅蜀，蜀亡則吳服，二方既定，然後遵舜、禹之軌，王從之。及至王薨，惇追恨前言，發病卒。孫盛評曰：夏侯惇恥為漢官，求受魏印，桓階方惇，有義直之節；考其傳記，世語為妄矣。
:::
:::
:::


## Jiàn'ān 25 (220) {.unnumbered}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Twenty-Fifth Year, Spring, Standard Moon [220 Feb 22 – Mar 21], reached Luòyáng. [Sūn] Quán struck and beheaded [Guān] Yǔ, sent his head.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
二十五年春正月，至洛陽。權擊斬羽，傳其首。
:::
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Gēngzǐ [220 Mar 15], the King passed away at Luòyáng, his years sixty-six. <a href="#annotation-118" id="source-118">[118]</a> Legacy Order  said: “Heaven’s Under is not yet secure and settled, and cannot follow the old ways. When the burial is complete, all are to remove mourning clothes. Those commanding troops in garrison camps are all to not leave their garrison departments. Relevant managers are to each continue in their offices. Dress in seasonal clothes, without storage of gold or jade treasures.”  Posthumous name Wǔ-wáng. 
Second Moon [220 Mar 22 – Apr 20] Dīngmǎo [220 Apr 11], buried at Gāolíng. <a href="#annotation-119" id="source-119">[119]</a>
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
庚子，王崩于洛陽，年六十六。〔一〕遺令曰：「天下尚未安定，未得遵古也。葬畢，皆除服。其將兵屯戍者，皆不得離屯部。有司各率乃職。斂以時服，無藏金玉珍寶。」諡曰武王。二月丁卯，葬高陵。〔二〕
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-118" id="annotation-118">[118]</a> Shìyǔ states: Tàizǔ from Hànzhōng reached Luòyáng, raised Jiànshǐ Hall, cut down Zhuólóng shrine,  but from the trees blood came out.

Cáo Mán zhuàn states: The King sent laborer Sū Yuè to move a pear tree.  Digging it, a root was damaged and out came blood. [Sū] Yuè reported the situation. The King personally went to see and hated it, believing it inauspicious, returned and therefore fell ill.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔一〕　世語曰：太祖自漢中至洛陽，起建始殿，伐濯龍祠而樹血出。曹瞞傳曰：王使工蘇越徙美梨，掘之，根傷盡出血。越白狀，王躬自視而惡之，以為不祥，還遂寢疾。
:::
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
<a href="#source-119" id="annotation-119">[119]</a> Wèi shū states: Tàizǔ personally took the reins of Within the Seas, weeded and razed the crowds of the evil, his deploying of armies and employing of brigades overall followed the methods of Sūn [Wǔ] and Wú [Qǐ],  but in taking advantage of situations and setting surprises, outwitting the enemy to secure victory, the transformations were like a deity. He personally composed military books of over a hundred thousand words, the various officers on campaign all consulted his Xīn shū in managing affairs.  Overseeing matters he also hand wrote dispatch directions, those that followed orders achieved victory, those that violated instructions suffered defeats. Facing the enemy lines, his thoughts were tranquil and at ease, as if not wishing to battle, however reaching the decisive opportunity to seize victory, his energy was overflowing, therefore every battle was certain to succeed, the army never only by fortune victorious. He understood men and excelled in observation, difficult to beguile with falseness, selected out Yú Jīn and Yuè Jìn from among the battle lines,  obtained Zhāng Liáo and Xú Huǎng from within defeated enemies,  all assisted the mandate and established achievements, ranked as famed officers. The rest that he selected out from the small and obscure, raised to be governors and administrators, cannot even be counted. Therefore he created a great enterprise, civil and martial together enacted, led the army for over thirty years, his hand did not set aside books, in daytime then discussing martial strategy, in the night then pondering the classics, when climbing up high certain to compose an ode, and when he made a new poem, he set it to pipes and strings, all becoming musical songs. His talent and strength surpassed men, hand shooting flying birds, personally capturing fierce beasts, once at Nánpí in one day shooting pheasants and obtaining sixty-three heads. Reaching to the building of Palace Residences, repairing of machines and weapons, none were not by his methods and models, all completely by his intentions. Elegant in nature and frugal, he did not enjoy flowery decoration, the Rear Palace clothes were not embroidered, his attendants’ shoes were not of two colors, his curtains and screens when damaged were patched, his bedding was for warmth, with no fringe decorations. In attacking cities and capturing towns, when obtaining beautiful things, then bestowed them all on those with achievements. For accomplished labors that should be rewarded, he did not begrudge a thousand gold. For those without achievements hoping for bestowment, the smallest fraction was not given. The Four Quarters sent tribute, he shared it together with his subordinates. He always believed the systems of ending arrangements and the numbers of burial shrouds were complicated and without benefit, vulgar and also excessive, and therefore in advance on his own regulated his final arrangements to clothes of four packages and nothing more. 

Fù-zǐ states: Tàizǔ regretted that marriages had become extravagant and presumptuous. When his daughters were matched to someone, all had black curtains, the accompanying maid servants did not exceed ten people.

Zhāng Huá’s Bówùzhì  states: In Hàn’s era, Ānpíng’s Cuī Yuàn, [Cuī] Yuàn’s son [Cuī] Shí,  Hóngnóng’s Zhāng Zhī, [Zhāng] Zhī’s younger brother [Zhāng] Chǎng  all excelled in cursive script,  and Tàizǔ was second to them. Huán Tán and Cài Yōng excelled in music,  Píngyì’s Shān Zǐdào, Wáng Jiǔzhēn, Guō Kǎi, and others excelled in wéiqí,  Tàizǔ all matched them in ability. Also he enjoyed cultivation methods, also understood medicine and pharmacology, attracted and gathered masters of technical arts,  Lújiāng’s Zuǒ Cí, Qiáo Prefecture’s Huà Tuó, Gānlíng’s Gān Shǐ, Yángchéng’s Xì Jiǎn, none did not all come.  Also he regularly ate yěgé of one chǐ, and also sometimes drank poisoned alcohol. 

Fù-zǐ states: At Hàn’s end of the kings and dukes many cast aside royal clothes, wore headscarves as fashion, and therefore the sorts as Yuán Shào and Cuī Jūn,  although they were military commanders, all wore silk headscarves. Wèi Tàizǔ because Heaven’s Under was in desolation, resources and wealth lacking and exhausted, imitated ancient leather caps, cut silk to make the cap,  in accordance with intentions for simplicity and ease and adapting to the times, using color to distinguish noble and lowly. To the present it is in use, and can be said to be a military appearance, not a stately appearance.

Cáo Mán zhuàn states: Tàizǔ as a man was frivolous and impulsive, without weighty prestige, enjoyed music, singers and performers at his side, always from day to night. He wore clothes of light raw silk, his body wearing girdle of small belt and purse, to hold hand scarf and small items, at times wearing cap to meet guests. Every time he conversed with someone, he would tease and joke, completely without holding back, and when pleased he would greatly laugh, to the extent that his head would be drenched in his cups on the table, dishes and food all dirtying his headscarf, his recklessness was like this. However in wielding law he was severe and oppressive, if among the various officers there was one with a strategy that surpassed his own, then he would use the law to execute them, reaching to past friends and old enemies, also all had none remaining. Those he condemned to death, then he would face them and shed tears and sigh in pain, but to the end none were spared. Previously, Yuán Zhōng  was Pèi Chancellor, once wished to use the law to punish Tàizǔ, and Pèi State’s Huán Shào  also disparaged him. Reaching to when he was at Yǎn Province, Chénliú’s Biān Ràng  in speaking comments often offended Tàizǔ, Tàizǔ killed him and clan exterminated his family. [Yuán] Zhōng and [Huán] Shào both fled the troubles to Jiāo Province. Tàizǔ sent an envoy to meet Administrator Shì Xiè  to completely clan exterminate them.  Huán Shào was able to surrender himself, bowed and apologized in the courtyards, Tàizǔ said: “Can kneeling pardon death?” Therefore killed him. Once he set out the army, traveled through wheat, ordered: “Soldiers are not to damage wheat, violators die.” Cavalry servicemen all dismounted horse, parting the wheat to support one another. Then Tàizǔ’s horse galloped into the wheat. Ordered the Registrar to discuss punishment. The Registrar replied believing: “By the principles of the Chūnqiū, punishments are not applied on the honored.”  Tàizǔ said: “To systemize a law but myself violate it, how can I command subordinates? However I am the army commander, and cannot kill myself, and request to punish myself.” Therefore he drew sword and cut his hair to set on the ground. Also he had a favored concubine that once accompanied when he napped during the day, pillowed on her lap, instructed her stating: “In a short while wake me.” The concubine saw Tàizǔ was resting peacefully, and did not at once wake him. When he woke up himself, had her beaten to death. Once while suppressing bandits, the government grain was not enough, and he privately said to the manager: “What can be done?” The manager said: “We can use smaller measuring cups to satisfy it.” Tàizǔ said: “Excellent.” Later those in the army said Tàizǔ was cheating the masses. Tàizǔ said to the manager: “I must specially rely on your death to appease the masses, if not the matter cannot be resolved.” Thus beheaded him, taking the head with an announcement sign stating: “For using smaller measuring cups, stealing government grain, beheaded him at the army gates.” His ruthless brutality and accommodating deceptions were all of this sort.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
〔二〕　魏書曰：太祖自統御海內，芟夷群醜，其行軍用師，大較依孫、吳之法，而因事設奇，譎敵制勝，變化如神。自作兵書十萬餘言，諸將征伐，皆以新書從事。臨事又手為節度，從令者克捷，違教者負敗。與虜對陳，意思安閒，如不欲戰，然及至決機乘勝，氣勢盈溢，故每戰必克，軍無幸勝。知人善察，難眩以偽，拔于禁、樂進於行陳之間，取張遼、徐晃於亡虜之內，皆佐命立功，列為名將；其餘拔出細微，登為牧守者，不可勝數。是以創造大業，文武並施，御軍三十餘年，手不捨書，晝則講武策，夜則思經傳，登高必賦，及造新詩，被之管絃，皆成樂章。才力絕人，手射飛鳥，躬禽猛獸，嘗于南皮一日射雉獲六十三頭。及造作宮室，繕治器械，無不為之法則，皆盡其意。雅性節儉，不好華麗，後宮衣不錦繡，侍御履不二采，帷帳屏風，壞則補納，茵蓐取溫，無有緣飾。攻城拔邑，得美麗之物，則悉以賜有功，勳勞宜賞，不吝千金，無功望施，分毫不與，四方獻御，與群下共之。常以送終之制，襲稱之數，繁而無益，俗又過之，故預自制終亡衣服，四篋而已。傅子曰：太祖愍嫁取之奢僭，公女適人，皆以皁帳，從婢不過十人。張華博物志曰：漢世，安平崔瑗、瑗子寔、弘農張芝、芝弟昶並善草書，而太祖亞之。桓譚、蔡邕善音樂，馮翊山子道、王九真、郭凱等善圍棋，太祖皆與埒能。又好養性法，亦解方藥，招引方術之士，廬江左慈、譙郡華佗、甘陵甘始、陽城郄儉無不畢至，又習啖野葛至一尺，亦得少多飲鴆酒。傅子曰：漢末王公，多委王服，以幅巾為雅，是以袁紹、（崔豹）〔崔鈞〕之徒，雖為將帥，皆著縑巾。魏太祖以天下凶荒，資財乏匱，擬古皮弁，裁縑帛以為帢，合于簡易隨時之義，以色別其貴賤，于今施行，可謂軍容，非國容也。曹瞞傳曰：太祖為人佻易無威重，好音樂，倡優在側，常以日達夕。被服輕綃，身自佩小鞶囊，以盛手巾細物，時或冠帢帽以見賓客。每與人談論，戲弄言誦，盡無所隱，及歡悅大笑，至以頭沒杯案中，肴膳皆沾汙巾幘，其輕易如此。然持法峻刻，諸將有計畫勝出己者，隨以法誅之，及故人舊怨，亦皆無餘。其所刑殺，輒對之垂涕嗟痛之，終無所活。初，袁忠為沛相，嘗欲以法治太祖，沛國桓邵亦輕之，及在兗州，陳留邊讓言議頗侵太祖，太祖殺讓，族其家，忠、邵俱避難交州，太祖遣使就太守士燮盡族之。桓邵得出首，拜謝於庭中，太祖謂曰：「跪可解死邪！」遂殺之。常出軍，行經麥中，令「士卒無敗麥，犯者死」。騎士皆下馬，付麥以相持，於是太祖馬騰入麥中，敕主簿議罪；主簿對以春秋之義，罰不加於尊。太祖曰：「制法而自犯之，何以帥下？然孤為軍帥，不可自殺，請自刑。」因援劍割髮以置地。又有幸姬常從晝寢，枕之臥，告之曰：「須臾覺我。」姬見太祖臥安，未即寤，及自覺，棒殺之。常討賊，廩穀不足，私謂主者曰：「如何？」主者曰：「可以小斛以足之。」太祖曰：「善。」後軍中言太祖欺眾，太祖謂主者曰：「特當借君死以厭眾，不然事不解。」乃斬之，取首題徇曰：「行小斛，盜官穀，斬之軍門。」其酷虐變詐，皆此類也。

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="70%"}
Appraisal states: At Hàn’s end, Heaven’s Under was in great chaos, the stalwart and powerful all rising, and Yuán Shào like a tiger oversaw four provinces,  his strength flourishing without match. Tàizǔ formulated strategies and enacted plans, thrashing within the world,  wielding the legalist techniques of Shēn [Bùhài] and Shāng [Yāng],  encompassing the exceptional strategies of Hán [Xìn] and Bái [Qǐ],  government office conferred by talents, each according to their abilities, discarding feelings in appointment and calculation, not caring for old grievances, that in the end he was able to wield Imperial power,  succeeded and achieved the vast enterprise, was only because his enlightened strategy was the most exceptional. It could be said that he was no ordinary man, a hero who transcended the era.
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
評曰：漢末，天下大亂，雄豪並起，而袁紹虎視四州，彊盛莫敵。太祖運籌演謀，鞭撻宇內，攬申、商之法術，該韓、白之奇策，官方授材，各因其器，矯情任算，不念舊惡，終能總御皇機，克成洪業者，惟其明略最優也。抑可謂非常之人，超世之傑矣。 
:::
:::
